methods.name: deepprofiler
methods.notes: Embedding is the activation of block6a_activation reduced over the spatial axes by successive mean(axis=1); 672 is the channel count of block6a_bn, not the model output (ClassProb is 490-way). Default in this project is block6a_activation -> 672; the upstream default of pool5 -> 1280 is available via feature_layer.

methods.name: ca_mae
methods.notes: Variable channel count is supported: pass channel_names matching the array you supply. return_channelwise_embeddings=True yields 384*C. Embeddings are reported to need batch correction (PCA-CenterScale or TVN) before comparison.

methods.name: cellclip
methods.notes: The released checkpoint consumes precomputed per-channel DINOv2-Giant embeddings (5 x 1536), NOT images. Extracting those embeddings is a separate upstream stage requiring DINOv2-Giant, which is not bundled. The text tower (BERT) is inside the checkpoint but unused for image embedding.

methods.name: o2vae
methods.notes: Official MEF weights.  Paper: Burgess J, Nirschl JJ, Zanellati M-C, Lozano A, Cohen S, Yeung-Levy S. "Orientation-invariant autoencoders learn robust representations for shape profiling of cells and organelles." Nature Communications 15, 1022 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41467-024-45362-4; code github.com/jmhb0/o2vae (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10206848).  ("mefs" = Mouse Embryonic Fibroblasts.)  Input is a SINGLE-CHANNEL binary cell silhouette at 64x64 in [0,1] -- O2-VAE is a shape model, so for Cell Painting it consumes a mask derived from the DNA channel rather than 5-channel intensity.  That modality difference is inherent to the method, not a handling choice, and must be stated whenever it is compared against intensity models.  DOMAIN SHIFT WARNING: the official checkpoint was trained on CELL silhouettes (configs/config_mefs.py:19, data_dir=.../data/mefs/scaled/cell) and no separate nucleus checkpoint is published, so feeding it a NUCLEUS silhouette is out-of-domain inference and the embedding distribution does not match the training distribution.  Also note the paper text says "embedding dimensions d = 128" while the released checkpoint measures zdim=512 (q_net.fully_net.3.bias is (1024,)); the code and the weights are authoritative.

methods.name: unidino
methods.license: BSD-3-Clause (code, README:108) / CC BY-NC 4.0 (weights, README:110; GitHub API reports CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0)
methods.notes: Single-channel model; the multi-channel output is per-channel embeddings concatenated in input order (source/inference_utils.py:29-34), so the result is 384 * C and IS order-sensitive (measured: a channel permutation changes the vector by up to 2.109).  The scale is declared: `source/image_ops.py:14-20` divides by 2**16-1, so the input must be uint16 -- an 8-bit crop is rejected with reason='value-range' rather than silently divided into a black image.  Weights 1.38 GB on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14988837), ~9 KB/s here (~43 h).  [SURROGATE] The checkpoint loaded here was trained on this repository's demo crops by scripts/embedding_benchmark/train_surrogates.py; the authors' weights could not be obtained. The architecture and the input/output contract are the published ones, so the interface is exercised for real -- but any score is NOT this method's published performance and must never be compared against one.

methods.name: morphogenie
methods.notes: Weights only on Google Drive, unreachable here.  The official extraction path is non-deterministic (see determinism).  Its centring preprocessing is MATLAB -- and the MATLAB SOURCE IS IN THE OFFICIAL REPOSITORY, at ImagePreProcessing/MultipleCells/CPA/GetCentImages.m; what is missing here is the MATLAB runtime, Cellpose and the raw data, not the code.  Measured: the MATLAB crop is 200x200 (GetCentImages.m:26, `Crop=[Centerx-100, Centery-100, 200, 200]`) and is min-max stretched to uint8 there (:38); the 256x256 resize happens on the Python side (gan_training/utils.py:352-357, Resize + Normalize(0.5)).  So the method is not reproducible from the repository alone -- but the reason is the missing runtime and data, not missing code.  The shipped default is nc=3 (RGB); no Cell Painting example is provided upstream.  [SURROGATE] The checkpoint loaded here was trained on this repository's demo crops by scripts/embedding_benchmark/train_surrogates.py; the authors' weights could not be obtained. The architecture and the input/output contract are the published ones, so the interface is exercised for real -- but any score is NOT this method's published performance and must never be compared against one.
